 In Re : Cran 1 of 2025
This application has been filed, praying for an appropriate  order in view of the subsequent developments during the pendency  of the revisional application, being CRR No. 598 of 2025.
A dispute arose between the petitioners and the O.p. no.2 in  relation to a commercial transaction between them.

As a result of  the said dispute, four criminal cases were initiated, of which three  were filed by O.P. No. 2 against the present petitioners, and one was  instituted by the petitioners against O.P. No. 2
Mr. Singh, learned Senior Advocate representing the  petitioners, submits that O.P. No. 2 initially lodged a complaint  before the Tamluk Police Station on 12.04.2023.

Based on the said  complaint, Tamluk Police Station Case No. 387 of 2023 dated CRR/598/2025 on 7 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/84056268/
1  2 12.04.2023 , under Sections 420/406/468/506/34 of the Indian Penal Code, was registered against the present petitioners.
Upon completion of investigation, a final report, vide FRMF No. 575 of 2023 dated 13.07.2023, was submitted.
Aggrieved thereby, O.P. No. 2 / de facto complainant filed a petition under Section 173(8) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, commonly known as a Naraji Petition .
The said petition is still pending final adjudication.

Subsequently based on the self-same facts, the de facto complainant lodged another complaint before the Bhawanipur Police Station which led to registration of Bhawanipur Police Station Case No. 94 dated 09.04.2024.
Petitioners filed a revisional application being CRR 4847 of 2024 before this Hon ble Court with a prayer for quashing of this case.

A co-ordinate Bench of this Court, by passing an interim order, directed that the investigation of this case will proceed; however, no coercive action shall be taken against the petitioners until 31st March, 2025 or until further orders,
whichever is earlier.
He further submits that the interim order was extended from time to time and is still in force.
The O.P. no.2 subsequently lodged another complaint at Tamluk Police Station, on the basis of which Tamluk Police Station Case No. 1031 of 2024 dated 22.11.2024 was registered.

entities.text: Tamluk Police Station Case No. 1031 of 2024
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: He also submits that the petitioners filed an application seeking pre-arrest bail, which was registered as CRM(A) 1251 of 2025.

He further submits that, taking note of the fact that the O.P. no.2 had filed three cases against the petitioners based substantially on similar facts, the benefit of pre-arrest bail was extended in favour of the petitioners.
He informs the Court that a charge-sheet has been filed against O.P. No. 2 in the case instituted by the petitioners.

He also submits that in connection with the last case i.e. Tamluk Police Station Case No. 1031 of 2024, ten accounts of the petitioners maintained in different banks across the State have been freezed.
He also submits that since those accounts have been freezed, the petitioners  business has been seriously hampered.
He further submits that a direction should be given upon the concerned bank or investigating officer to take necessary steps so that those accounts can be de-freezed.

He draws my attention to the report submitted by the investigating officer before the court of the learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Tamluk, where the investigating officer has categorically stated that those accounts were not directly involved in this case.

entities.text: court of the learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Tamluk
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Mr. Bardhan, learned Advocate, duly assisted by Mr. Jana, learned Advocate, representing the State,
concurs with the submissions made by Mr. Singh on behalf of the petitioners that upon enquiry the investigating officer found that the accounts which were previously freezed were not involved in the case registered as Tamluk Police Station Case No. 1031 of 2024.

Heard the learned Advocates representing the respective parties and perused the materials on record.

Admittedly, a co-ordinate Bench of this Court, in its order dated 29.04.2024, passed in CRM (A)
1251 of 2024, observed that the de facto complainant (O.P. no. 2 herein) has, in fact, filed three cases against the petitioners substantially on similar facts.

"Therefore, it prima facie appears that the doctrine of sameness may be applicable to the present case, being Tamluk Police Station Case No. 1031 of 2024, in connection with which the I.O. took steps to freeze the accounts.

entities.text: Tamluk Police Station Case No. 1031 of 2024
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, the possibility of the application of the doctrine of sameness, and the conclusion arrived at by the concerned Investigating Officer, that the accounts of the petitioners, which were earlier frozen in connection with the said case, are not directly involved, I find merit in the petitioners  contention.

Accordingly, this application, being CRAN 1 of 2025, is disposed of by directing the Investigating Officer to take necessary steps to de-freeze the petitioners  accounts,
thereby enabling the petitioners to operate the said accounts without any hindrance or restriction.
Investigating officer is directed to act on the basis of the server copy of this order without insisting on production of the certified copy of this order by the petitioners.

In Re : CRR 598 of 2025 Having heard the learned Advocates representing the petitioners and the State and upon perusal of the materials on record, I am of the view that the issue raised in the present revisional application needs to be addressed and resolved after affording an opportunity of hearing to the O.P. no. 2.

In view thereof, the petitioners are directed to serve a copy of this application along with all annexures thereto and the connected application, if any, to the O.P. no.2 and file affidavit-of-service on the returnable date.

As it has been held that considering the facts and circumstances of the case doctrine of sameness be applied, I am inclined to pass an interim order that investigation of this case will go on; however, no coercive step shall be taken against the petitioners until the end of September, 2025 or until further orders, whichever is earlier.
List this matter on 4th September, 2025, under the heading "Fixed Matters".

(Partha Sarathi Chatterjee, J.)
